title: Console hot-path stream adapter and micro-aggregator for real-time metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Implement a streaming adapter and small-window micro-aggregator for console metrics to enable sub-second dashboards and alerting. This ticket covers the hot-path processors that ingest per-token and per-request telemetry from the API gateway, perform lightweight enrichment and tenant-aware aggregation, and forward compact rollups to downstream stores (real-time metrics tier + long-term analytics).

Goals:
- Deliver <200ms end-to-end processing for common request paths under steady load.
- Ensure at-least-once ingestion with idempotent downstream writes; provide strategy for dedup and eventual exactly-once where needed.
- Support per-tenant sampling, 1s/5s sliding-window micro-aggregations, and per-route latency quantiles.
- Low operational overhead: bounded memory per partition and clear backpressure behavior.

Out of scope: wide-window historical aggregation (handled by batch jobs), UI changes to dashboards (separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Hot-path service deployed behind feature flag and processing synthetic traffic at target latency (<200ms median).
Aggregates for 1s and 5s windows written to realtime metrics topic and visible in staging dashboards.
Graceful backpressure: input queue size capped; excess requests are rejected with meter and fallback routing to cold path.
End-to-end test demonstrating idempotent writes after simulated retries and restarts.
Runbook and a basic SLO page (p95 processing latency <500ms, error rate <0.1%) published.
